title: Discuss sprinkler planning for branching and pod development
detail: ICAR-IIPR reports a study comparing sprinkler irrigation at branching plus pod development against branching alone. Discuss whether this stage-based approach fits your field, recent rain and available supply; no dose or yield benefit is predicted for your farm.
timing: At branching or pod development, before deciding the next watering
sourceCondition: Chickpea research finding; local soil, recent rain and equipment suitability need confirmation.

title: Discuss the critical stage for your limited irrigation
detail: The ICAR-IIMR rabi-sorghum guide discusses flower-primordial or boot-leaf stages when water permits only one irrigation, depending on soil moisture. Confirm the stage and field moisture before deciding; the app does not prescribe an amount.
timing: At the boot-leaf stage, before using the limited supply
sourceCondition: Rabi sorghum, limited irrigation and soil-moisture-dependent timing; not kharif instructions.

title: Discuss protecting crown-root initiation
detail: The ICAR-IIWBR pocket guide prioritizes crown-root initiation in its one-irrigation schedule. Discuss whether this applies to your crop and current soil moisture before allocating the supply.
timing: At crown-root initiation, before committing the available irrigation
sourceCondition: Wheat with only one irrigation available; local soil and current conditions require confirmation.

source.title: ICAR-IIWBR · Wheat Cultivation in India
source.section: Irrigation schedule under different water availability

title: Discuss irrigation at a moisture-sensitive wheat stage
detail: The ICAR-IIWBR guide identifies crown-root initiation and flowering as especially sensitive to moisture stress. Use the confirmed stage, field moisture and remaining supply to discuss a local irrigation plan; no schedule or dose is inferred here.
sourceCondition: Wheat critical-stage guidance; this does not imply that a regional surface model measures root-zone adequacy.

title: Discuss the district’s low-recharge wheat/chickpea options
detail: The historical Ahmednagar contingency table lists wheat and/or chickpea under insufficient groundwater recharge for open-well irrigation on medium/deep black soil. It also discusses critical-stage irrigation for wheat and sprinkler irrigation for chickpea. This is an option to review locally, not an instruction to change crop.
timing: Before buying seed or committing area
sourceCondition: Insufficient groundwater recharge due to low rainfall; open-well irrigated medium/deep black soil.

title: Review the district’s historical gram alternatives
detail: The Aurangabad plan’s low-groundwater-recharge table lists retaining chickpea or considering BDN-9-3, Akash, Vijay or Vikas in its stated medium/deep black-soil farming situation. Check current local suitability and availability; these historical names are not a current variety recommendation.
timing: Before selecting seed; obtain current local confirmation
sourceCondition: Insufficient groundwater recharge; medium/deep black soil in the source’s assured/high-rainfall farming situation, which must be checked locally.

title: Review the district’s critical-stage water contingency
detail: The historical Hingoli low-recharge table retains wheat and refers to irrigation at critical growth stages for its medium/deep black-soil farming situation. Confirm the source conditions and current crop stage locally before applying that contingency.
sourceCondition: Insufficient groundwater recharge; source’s medium/deep black-soil assured/high-rainfall farming situation still needs local confirmation.
